source: Realtor.com analysis, Nov. 24, 2026; Freddie Mac PMMS

headline: Saving for a home
now takes *a decade*
slides.fig_caption: To save a 10% down payment on a median-priced home
slides.sub: Back in the 1980s, it took just over three years.

slides.title: Why the math *got harder*
points: Home prices: about 3x household income then, closer to *5x* now.
Savings rate: near 10% then, about *5%* now.
Lower rates today don't offset bigger prices and thinner savings.

slides.label: more *yearly income* the typical household needs to buy
slides.body: Realtor.com puts the typical household's lost home purchasing power at about $150,000.

slides.label: average *30-year fixed* rate ahead of Thanksgiving
slides.body: Down from 7.28% last week, per Freddie Mac. A year ago the average was 6.23%.

slides.title: Answer the *dinner question*
slides.body: Many renters will hear 'why haven't you bought yet?' this week. Meet them with a realistic timeline, a lender intro and local numbers, not pressure. Those talks can turn into 2027 clients.
